A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same single-image VD-RAG poisoning work. All 19 pages of v2 and 25 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable; text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the figures, tables and equations.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval, generation, transferability, ablation and defense experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original white-box and black-box attack experiments, defense evaluations and supplementary results, including five-starting-image summaries.

M1.justification: The underlying MO-PGD objectives, three targeted settings, universal attack, prompt-generated attacks, transfer attacks, ensemble optimization and adaptive defense attacks already appear in v2. v3 reorganizes and formalizes these procedures without establishing an underlying algorithm change; the newly printed update equation has a separate mathematical issue noted under T1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ViDoRe-V1-AI and ViDoRe-V2-ESG, universal attacks, and the same three targeted tasks: one query, five related queries sharing an answer, and two queries with distinct answers. Added victim models and ensemble configurations do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The GPT-4o image-generation baseline evaluated in v2 is replaced by GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Flash prompt-based comparators in v3. These participate in the reported targeted and universal comparisons. GPT-4o remains involved in constructing malicious target answers.

E3.justification: The reported optimization budget changes from 500 to 250 gradient steps. v3 adds InternVL3-2B, expands targeted Settings II/III beyond SmolVLM, extends knowledge-expansion evaluations beyond CLIP-L, and introduces ensemble evaluations excluding the target models. Main comparisons also stop separately reporting exact-match ASR-G-Hard, emphasizing semantic similarity instead.

E4.justification: v3 adds explicit tests of ensemble transfer to excluded target models, broadens existing defense analyses, and supplies prompt-generated attack case studies in Figures 4–5. The ColPali ablation, perturbation sensitivity study, UMAP analysis and adaptive judge attacks already exist in v2 and should not be counted as new.

E5.justification: v3 newly documents five runs using different initial images and reports means and maxima across them; v2 specifies an arbitrary starting image without repeated-run summaries. This adds replication and aggregation information, but neither version supplies standard deviations, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised and expanded. For example, targeted ColPali–SmolVLM ASR-R@1 changes from 1.000 in v2 Table 3 to a five-image mean of 0.60 in v3 Table 1. New generator, prompt-comparator and excluded-model ensemble results appear, while detailed transfer tables become aggregated categories. Given the changed budget and aggregation, these are revised results rather than demonstrated same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: v3 adds an explicit update equation (4) that is inconsistent with its stated loss minimization: it adds the positive gradient and clips individual increments rather than the total perturbation. v2 describes PGD without this inconsistent formula. The original retrieval/generation objectives and UMAP mathematics are otherwise retained; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v3 elevates black-box attack coverage to an explicit contribution and distinguishes targeted black-box success from universal black-box failure in the abstract and conclusion. The ColPali ablation disappears from the contribution list but remains in the paper. The central single-image VD-RAG poisoning claim is retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds discussion of difficulty balancing retrieval and generation objectives, qualifies ensemble effectiveness, and expands limitations to untested JPEG compression and watermarking. It also discusses the success–stealth tradeoff of injecting multiple images. Earlier majority-vote and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds approximately 325 GPU hours of compute information and a concrete prompt-based image-generation example in Appendix F. Hardware, the code/configuration/results repository, and judge prompts were already disclosed in v2; relocating the repository link does not change resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations concerning Nougat, Agent Smith, malicious-user-prompt defenses and model fingerprinting, while removing citations including MARAGE. Positioning more explicitly emphasizes document-specific datasets and modern retrievers. The principal distinction from text-image-pair RAG poisoning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten. Pipeline and attack descriptions become a consolidated section with an explicit attacker-knowledge taxonomy; targeted attacks precede universal attacks; related work moves near the end; and appendices are reorganized. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond added experimental content.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document template and extensively restructures tables with grouped retrieval/generation headings, mean/max columns and baseline differences. Defense tables are merged and expanded, prompt-generated examples are added, and the existing UMAP figures are regrouped into Figure 6. The underlying UMAP and perturbation plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Five-starting-image reporting, broader model and baseline comparisons, and clearer attacker-knowledge distinctions improve empirical support and interpretability. Added prompt and compute details also help reproducibility. These gains are limited by the inconsistent update formula in v3 Eq. 4 and unrevised claims of perfect universal retrieval despite Table 4 reporting CLIP-L means of 0.90–0.98, making the net improvement modest.
